method: Labs 0.9.0, eight fresh-process blocks per case, serial round-robin case execution. Timings cover a full 10k-entity invocation. Summary uses the median of block medians, not pooled sample averages. Heap deltas are Labs per-invocation p50, not retained memory or proof of zero allocation. Retained memory is recorded separately in cleanup-memory-results.json. Source fingerprints hash sorted relative path, NUL, file SHA256 and newline.
decision: Kept separate numeric and prepared value-write hot paths after a shared row-write helper regressed prepared throughput by about 10%. Kept consolidated change publication, spawn initialization, ordinary trait removal, storage preparation and borrowed entity iteration. Query plans own matching, visits own workspaces and borrow lifetimes. No contract or storage-layout changes.
limitations: The initial 35-case runs had clock drift and several apparent slowdowns also appeared in unchanged Iris controls. Focused before/after cases therefore ran within the same Labs schedule.
All four final focused comparisons are neutral at the Labs 5% minimum-effect threshold. One after tag-toggle run has high tail latency, so this is not a tail-latency equivalence claim.
The full 35-case candidate uses the initial cleanup source. The final source only restores separate scalar write paths. These writes were remeasured in the focused run.

Retained plan-only heap readings varied substantially across fresh processes. Do not interpret their median difference as a memory saving. ArrayBuffer retention was identical for every before/after shape.
